item.research_question: How does Al alloying influence the tensile behavior, deformation mechanisms, and fracture modes of a Co-rich Co40Fe25Cr20Ni15 high-entropy alloy?
item.processing_route: Arc-melting raw elemental pellets, casting into a 50 mm × 20 mm × 4 mm mold, homogenization at 1423 K for 2 h, water quenching, cold-rolling with 70% thickness reduction, and recrystallization annealing at 973 K, 1023 K, and 1123 K for 2 h followed by water quenching.
item.test_conditions: Room-temperature tensile tests using a computer-controlled universal tensile testing machine at a strain rate of 10−4 s−1; Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations at 300 K.
key_findings: The addition of 5 at.% Al increased the strength-ductility product (UTS × εf) from 19.2 GPa·% (0Al-1123 K) to 41.2 GPa·% (5Al-1123 K).
The 5Al-1123 K sample achieved a yield strength of 405 ± 4 MPa, tensile strength of 830 ± 3 MPa, and fracture elongation of ~50%.
The 0Al-973 K sample exhibited the highest yield strength of 612 ± 8 MPa but the lowest fracture elongation of ~15%.
The intrinsic stacking fault energy (SFE) increased from 70.6 mJ/m² in the 0Al alloy to 81.1 mJ/m² in the 5Al alloy.
The slip energy barrier (Δγ) decreased from 275 mJ/m² in the 0Al alloy to 228 mJ/m² in the 5Al alloy.
The twinning propensity ratio (Λratio) increased from 1.18 in the 0Al alloy to 1.29 in the 5Al alloy.
The fracture mode shifted from a mixture of quasi-cleavage and ductile-dimple (0Al) to exclusively ductile dimple (5Al).
The twin fraction in the 5Al-1123 K sample (~15.3%) was higher than in the 0Al-1123 K sample (~9.2%) at comparable local strains.
item.mechanism: Al alloying increases the intrinsic SFE but reduces the slip energy barrier, which favors dislocation mobility and increases twinning propensity. This combination promotes prolonged strain hardening and delays necking, allowing for higher plastic strain accumulation and a transition to ductile dimple fracture, whereas the 0Al alloy suffers from high resistance to dislocation nucleation and limited slip mobility leading to early fracture.
item.limitations: The authors note that the calculated SFE values (70.6 and 81.1 mJ/m²) are relatively high compared to the proposed experimental range for mechanical twinning (15 ≤ SFE ≤ 45 mJ/m²), attributing this discrepancy to factors like thermodynamic, magnetic, ordering, temperature, and pressure effects that are difficult to replicate in theoretical calculations.
quotes: The addition of Al resulted in a massive improvement in the strength-ductility product, even at similar grain sizes, and also altered the fracture mode from quasi-cleavage to ductile dimple fracture.

The MD simulations revealed the SFE increased upon Al addition; however, the slip energy barrier was reduced, which favored the mobility of dislocations and twinning propensity to prolong strain hardening.
The γisf for the 0Al is found to be 70.6 mJ/m2 while it increases to 81.1 mJ/m2 for the 5Al sample.
